header.running_head: The Justice of Hadhrat Umar Farooq (RA)

blocks.text: Hadhrat Ubay (RA) continued, "I feel that Abbaas (RA) has a greater right to his house, which cannot be taken from him until he is pleased." Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) then said, "Since you have made the decision in my favour, I wish to make it Sadaqah for the Muslims." [^1]
The Incident of Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Umar bin Khattaab and Abu Saroo'ah

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that his brother Abdur Rahmaan and Abu Saroo'ah both drank some wine while they were in Egypt during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Umar (RA). They were both intoxicated and the following morning they approached Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) who was the Ameer of Egypt. They said to him, "Purify us (by imposing the penalty) because we had both become intoxicated with what we drank."
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "When my brother mentioned to me that he had become intoxicated, I said to him, 'Come into the house and I will purify you.' I did not know then that he had already been to Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA). When my brother told me that he had already informed the Ameer of Egypt, I said, 'Your head will not be shaved in front of all the people today. Go into the house and I will myself shave your head.' The practice of governors in those days was that they shaved the heads of criminals together with imposing the penalty. The two men then entered the house. I shaved my brother's head with my own hand and then Hadhrat Amr (RA) had them lashed."
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) continues, "When Hadhrat Umar (RA) heard about this, he wrote to Hadhrat Amr (RA) with instructions to send Abdur Rahmaan to him on a carriage. Hadhrat Amr (RA) complied and when Abdur Rahmaan reached (his father) Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA) lashed him and punished him further because of his relationship with him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then let him go and he lived hail and healthily for a month after which his predestination caught up with him and he passed away. Although people commonly believe that he died because of the lashing he received from Hadhrat Umar (RA), it is evident that he did not die because of this lashing." [^2]
